newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Polifin sees real earnings growth in H2.
newsitem.headline: Polifin sees real earnings growth in H2.

text.p: Polifin Ltd, the South African-based Sasol-AECI joint venture, said on Monday it expected real growth in earnings in the six months to June 1997 despite an anticipated further decrease in the oil price.

"The tax rate will go up but at an earnings level we are confidently anticipating a better than real return," managing director Trevor Munday told a news briefing at the group's half year results presentation.

Munday said international polymer markets were characterised by steady conditions during then six months to December 25 1996. The higher oil price which prevailed during that period had resulted in international monomer prices increasing and polymer prices either strengthening or stabilising.

Local feedstock costs had increased as a result of the rise in the oil price and a further deterioration in the rand/dollar exchange rate. Monomer and polymer prices moved marginally up, reflecting international trends and -- partly -- the weaker rand.
"The oil price has (since) softened and may decrease further once the northern hemisphere winter is over," Munday said.

International monomer and polymer prices should move in sympathy with a lower oil price towards the end of the coming six months, he added, but he still expected real growth in earnings in the second six months.
Polifin increased turnover by 11 percent to 1.8 billion rand for the six months to December 25 while earnings per share and dividends rose by 20 percent.
Total borrowing at December 25 1996 dropped to 207 million rand, representing a gearing of 13 percent, Munday said.
"We forecast gearing to be down to the 10 percent mark by the end of the present financial year at the end of June," he added.
